knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/problem:
Find the slope $m'$ of the normal line to the curve

$$
y=-3x^{2}+4x
$$

at the point $\left(-1,-7\right)$. Give an exact answer.

$m'=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=-3x^{2}+4x$.

Apply the power rule:

$$
f'(x)=-6x+4
$$

The tangent slope at $\left(-1,-7\right)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
m=f'(-1)&=-6\left(-1\right)+4\\
&=6+4\\
&=10
\end{aligned}
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so take the negative reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}
m'&=-\frac{1}{m}\\
&=-\frac{1}{\left(10\right)}\\
&=-\frac{1}{10}
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the slope $m'$ of the normal line to the curve

$$
y=(x-3)(x^{2}+x)
$$

at the point $\left(1,-4\right)$. Give an exact answer.

$m'=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=(x-3)(x^{2}+x)$. Expand and combine like terms before differentiating.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=x^{3}+x^{2}-3x^{2}-3x\\
&=x^{3}-2x^{2}-3x
\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the power rule:

$$
f'(x)=3x^{2}-4x-3
$$

The tangent slope at $\left(1,-4\right)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
m=f'(1)&=3\left(1\right)^{2}-4\left(1\right)-3\\
&=3-4-3\\
&=-4
\end{aligned}
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so take the negative reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}
m'&=-\frac{1}{m}\\
&=-\frac{1}{\left(-4\right)}\\
&=\frac{1}{4}
\end{aligned}
$$

Find where the normal line to the curve $y=x^{2} - x$ at the point $(-1,2)$ intersects the $x$-axis.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate the polynomial.

$$
f'(x)=2 x - 1.
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(-1)&=2 (-1) - 1=-3, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(-3)}=\frac{1}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(-1,2)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(2)&=\frac{1}{3}(x-(-1)), \\y&=\frac{x}{3} + \frac{7}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=\frac{1}{3}x+\left(\frac{7}{3}\right), \\x&=-7.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $(-7,0)$.

question.:question/problem:
Find where the normal line to the curve $y=x^{3} + 2$ at the point $(1,3)$ intersects the $y$-axis.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate the polynomial.

$$
f'(x)=3 x^{2}.
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(1)&=3 (1)^{2}=3, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(3)}=- \frac{1}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(1,3)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(3)&=- \frac{1}{3}(x-(1)), \\y&=- \frac{x}{3} + \frac{10}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=- \frac{1}{3}\cdot 0+\left(\frac{10}{3}\right), \\y&=\frac{10}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $\left(0,\frac{10}{3}\right)$.

question.:question/problem:
Find where the normal line to the curve $y=x^{2} - 2 x - 2$ at the point $(-1,1)$ intersects the $y$-axis.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate the polynomial.

$$
f'(x)=2 x - 2.
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(-1)&=2 (-1) - 2=-4, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(-4)}=\frac{1}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(-1,1)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(1)&=\frac{1}{4}(x-(-1)), \\y&=\frac{x}{4} + \frac{5}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=\frac{1}{4}\cdot 0+\left(\frac{5}{4}\right), \\y&=\frac{5}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $\left(0,\frac{5}{4}\right)$.

question.:question/problem:
Find where the normal line to the curve $y=x^{3}$ at the point $(2,8)$ intersects the $x$-axis.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate the polynomial.

$$
f'(x)=3 x^{2}.
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(2)&=3 (2)^{2}=12, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(12)}=- \frac{1}{12}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(2,8)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(8)&=- \frac{1}{12}(x-(2)), \\y&=- \frac{x}{12} + \frac{49}{6}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=- \frac{1}{12}x+\left(\frac{49}{6}\right), \\x&=98.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $(98,0)$.

question.:question/problem:
Find where the normal line to the curve $y=-4\sqrt{x}-2x$ at the point with $x$-coordinate $4$ intersects the $y$-axis.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First find the point on the curve.

$$
f(4)=-4\sqrt{(4)}-2(4)=-16.
$$

The normal passes through $(4,-16)$.

Rewrite the radical or reciprocal using powers, then differentiate.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=- 4 x^{\frac{1}{2}} - 2 x, \\f'(x)&=-2 - \frac{2}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}=-2 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(4)&=-2 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{(4)}}=-3, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(-3)}=\frac{1}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(4,-16)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(-16)&=\frac{1}{3}(x-(4)), \\y&=\frac{x}{3} - \frac{52}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=\frac{1}{3}\cdot 0+\left(- \frac{52}{3}\right), \\y&=- \frac{52}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $\left(0,- \frac{52}{3}\right)$.

question.:question/problem:
Find where the normal line to the curve $y=2\sqrt{x}+3x$ at the point with $x$-coordinate $1$ intersects the $x$-axis.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First find the point on the curve.

$$
f(1)=2\sqrt{(1)}+3(1)=5.
$$

The normal passes through $(1,5)$.

Rewrite the radical or reciprocal using powers, then differentiate.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=2 x^{\frac{1}{2}} + 3 x, \\f'(x)&=3 + \frac{1}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}=3 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(1)&=3 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{(1)}}=4, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(4)}=- \frac{1}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(1,5)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(5)&=- \frac{1}{4}(x-(1)), \\y&=- \frac{x}{4} + \frac{21}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=- \frac{1}{4}x+\left(\frac{21}{4}\right), \\x&=21.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $(21,0)$.
